## Fresh Developments (Last 24-72h)

*Note: MU Q3 blowout, AVGO/OpenAI Jalapeño, and HIVE $220M GPU contract were covered in yesterday's report. Below focuses on new moves since June 26-27.*

**MRVL — S&P 500 Euphoria Erased by CFO Dump (June 26)**
Added to S&P 500 June 22 (+265% YTD). June 26: CFO sold 211K shares in a single day → stock -10% same day. Still under pressure. Context: MRVL acquired Celestial AI + XConn; NVIDIA invested $2B. The -10% CFO sell is technical/noise vs. the structural AI-connectivity thesis — but warrants a watch.

**STX — Sharp 12.2% Drop (June 26)**
Seagate dropped from $1,025 to $899.90 on June 26 on Equal-Weight downgrade citing SK Hynix HBM slowdown concerns as a read-through for HDD nearline demand. Context: CFO says firm orders cover 4-5 quarters; stock is +289% YTD. Likely overreaction. Yesterday's report covered the SK Hynix DDR5 pivot — this is the downstream echo.

**SNOW — +9.2% (June 27)**
Snowflake surged on Unlimitail Global Retail Media Data Hub partnership — a fresh AI data monetization use case. Buy consensus, analyst target ~$290.

**ZS — +6.2% (June 26)**
Partial recovery from -20% post FY27 guidance miss (16-17% vs. 18.4% expected), helped by Aston Martin F1 multi-year cybersecurity deal. YTD still -40%; fundamentals under scrutiny.

**SNDK — -13.6% (June 23), Volatile**
SanDisk (SNDK) is best S&P 500 performer YTD at +857% (data center revenue +233% QoQ). June 23 drop on South Korean memory weakness read-through. Extreme volatility is the story; no change to AI storage demand thesis.

**FSLR — Spike-and-Fade; Now at $239**
Hit 18-year intraday high ~$310 on Section 232 polysilicon tariff speculation (FSLR CdTe tech = exempt = net beneficiary). Since pulled back to $239 (June 26, -8.5% YTD) after Bernstein initiated Underperform June 16. Polysilicon prices still falling (CNY 33,200/ton, -0.02% WoW). Section 232 decision still pending.

**NVDA — Continued 10-Day Drift (-6%)**
No new hard negative. Trading ~$192-193. Custom ASIC narrative (Jalapeño) + market rotation weighing. Strong Buy consensus with $299 PT unchanged.

**Signals 1-4 (DRAM/HBM, Capex, AMD): No new prints since yesterday.** Baselines intact: Q2 DRAM +43-48% QoQ, HBM sold out through 2026, capex $725B, AMD Helios on-track Q3.

## Context (vs. Baseline)

HBM correction risk remains pushed to 2027-2028 (MU $100B contracts confirmed). MRVL -10% is an insider-selling event, not a thesis break; NVIDIA's $2B investment + Celestial AI/XConn acquisitions are still structural positives. STX pullback is a HDD-sentiment overhang from the SK Hynix DDR5 pivot story, not a demand-destruction signal. Solar policy catalyst (Section 232) still pending end of June.

## Most Important Development

**MRVL -10% on CFO dump** is today's cleanest actionable signal — insider selling into an S&P 500 inclusion pop. The structural AI-connectivity thesis (NVIDIA $2B investment, Celestial AI acquisition) is unchanged. Wash-out watch for a re-entry level. Secondary: **STX -12.2%** on HBM-read-through is likely an overreaction given 4-5 quarters of firm orders, but confirms the market is actively stress-testing memory names for any HBM correction signal.
